contract.interface:
The source targets chi(G)<=2h(G) for every finite simple graph, where h is complete-minor order. This universal target remains UNRESOLVED. For H on even N>=4 vertices and G=complement H, D=Delta(H), C=max_v induced-four-cycle incidence (each cycle once), set L=(1-x)^D(1-y)^C for x,y in(0,1). Conditions 1/(N-1)<=xL^2 and 1/[(N-1)(N-3)]<=yL^4 certify a pairwise-touching perfect matching of G and hence h(G)>=N/2. Uniform complete-graph matching bad events are forbidden H edges and the two diagonals of induced H four-cycles. Established canonical-event negative dependency and the lopsided local lemma are substantive imports, not a newly invented local lemma.

For Delta(H)=o(N) and limsup C/N^2<1/(4e), scalar activities x=A/N,y=B/N^2 work eventually. The 1/(4e) constant is a sufficient activity threshold, not an optimal graph threshold. Rooted extension retains connected disjoint touching bags B_i and unused even U: forbid F=complement G[U] union all K_{S_i}, S_i={u:no G-neighbour in B_i}. Use Delta(F) for first-kind events but induced cycles of complement G[U] for C. This extends the model to order r+|U|/2 only when the explicit budgets hold. No theorem acquires those budgets from high chromatic number.

An exact pin-release operation starts with uniform matching conditional on ab: choose x uniformly outside a; if x=b retain, otherwise replace ab,xy by ax,by. Its inverse is unique. Release multiple pins excluding still-pinned endpoints. New edges meet original pin support, so no disjoint-support canonical bad event is newly created. This belongs to established resampling-oracle machinery. The bijection alone proves no repeated-repair convergence or runtime bound.

For sufficiently large q=2^(2h+1), N=q^4, a modified published Suzuki-Tits line construction fixes a balanced bipartition on one parallel class and randomizes the other line labels. Source claims alpha(G_q)=2, chi(G_q)=N/2, an all-size-two K_(N/2) model, and no dominating model of order ceil((1/2-delta)N) for an absolute delta>0. The conclusion is h>=chi, not equality. Imported graph geometry and dominating-obstruction hypotheses remain explicit. Noncollinear codegrees=(1/4+o(1))q^2; at most two witnesses involve fixed lines. In triangle-free H, c_H(v)=sum_{w!=v}binom(codegree(v,w),2), with no extra factor; C<=(1/32+o(1))N^2 and D=O(q^3) satisfy the contact criterion. Balanced sides, codegree lower bounds and alpha(H)<2q^3 preserve the published deterministic obstruction. This asymptotic construction was not executed by the finite scripts.

Two K4 joined by one bridge have alpha=2,chi=h=4, nine legal perfect matchings and no pairwise-touching perfect matching. A bridge matching leaves odd unmatched sides; each legal matching has an edge away from the bridge on each side. A singleton K4 model still exists. Exhaustive pair-only coverage is strictly stronger than the desired minor theorem and cannot be repaired just by better scalar constants.

A distinct unproved proposal asks whether every vertex-chromatic-critical graph J has a partition into connected induced bipartite bags whose quotient Q is perfect. If so chi(J)<=2chi(Q)=2omega(Q)<=2h(J), and deleting chromatically redundant vertices proves the universal target. Entire-graph versions are false. For the specific Scott-Seymour-Wood recursive family A(k,r), source derives chi=omega=1+2k(k^2-1)/3+k(r-1), retaining a full-chromatic clique. Deletion removes that family's partition obstruction; the published entire-graph counterexample remains intact. Critical graphs have no nontrivial clique cutset. The property is closed under Mycielski for graphs without isolated vertices: root plus all shadows is an induced star, giving a perfect quotient cone. Neither fact classifies all critical graphs. Producer witnesses for18 critical atlas graphs and99 generated examples are finite tests, with repeated isomorphism types, not a universal proof.

The fractional-minor assertion chi(G)<=max_{J minor G}chi_f(J) is equivalent to exact Hadwiger. A minor-minimal k-chromatic nonclique J on n>k has chi_f(J)<=n(k-1)/(n-1)<k from J-v colour classes, while all proper minors have smaller chromatic number. Thus this proposed shortcut simply restates a harder target.
